To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ferumoxide and ferumoxides are efficient and long lasting labels for mesenchymal stem cells, and that protamine is the preferred carrier for ferumoxide.
ferumoxides labeled MSCs with protamine are efficiently visualized by in vivo MRI and maintain proliferation and viability for 7 days.

we have shown that rat and mouse MSCs can be efficiently labeled with SPIONs and that the labeled cells maintain proliferation and differentiation potential in vitro, and that these cells can be visualized in vivo by MRI.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an efficient and safe labeling protocol that will be useful in the study of stem cell therapy.
the optimization of the labeling of MSCs with SPIONs and the in vitro characterization of the biological properties of labeled MSCs.
the optimization of the labeling procedure of MSCs with ferumoxide, and the development of a protocol for in vivo cell tracking by MRI.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of ferumoxides with protamine is the most efficient, non-toxic method to label and visualize MSCs in vivo with MRI.
ferumoxide labeling of rat and mouse MSCs with protamine chlorhydrate is a reliable method for in vivo MRI tracking.
ferumoxide-labled MSCs are a good candidate for cell tracking by MRI.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ferumoxide-laden rat and mouse mesenchymal stem cells could be tracked in vivo for up to 21 days using MRI.
ferumoxide labeling of MSCs is a safe and effective method for cell labeling and in vivo tracking.
the use of protamine as a transfection agent for ferumoxide uptake into MSCs may provide the best method for cell tracking by MRI.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ferumoxides can be safely used for labeling MSCs for in vivo tracking with MRI, without compromising their proliferation, viability or differentiation potential.
the combination of ferumoxide and the cationic polypeptides PLL and protamine can be used to efficiently and safely label cells for MRI tracking.
ferumoxide-labled cells can be used for in vivo cell tracking with MRI.
